Analysis: Hypothesis 1 offers a well-integrated model linking tumor stress, exosome-mediated communication, and macrophage reprogramming. It leverages targeted methodologies (e.g., single-cell transcriptomics, CRISPR screens) that make it relatively straightforward to design experiments despite gaps in mechanistic specificity, and it addresses cancer immunomodulation—a critical and high-impact area. In contrast, Hypothesis 2, while novel in integrating viral infection stress, tRNA demethylation, and noncanonical Argonaute complexes, suffers from broader mechanistic ambiguities and an overambitious scope that complicates testability and risks conflating diverse outcomes. Moreover, Hypothesis 2 requires additional evidence to support key causal links. Overall, Hypothesis 1 is more plausible, better defined for testing, and presents lower risks in terms of safety and experimental complexity.
